h1: The 8 Best USB-C Docking Stations of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best USB-C Docking Stations: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the best USB-C docking stations for 2026, compared on display support, power delivery wattage and port count.
summary: The UGREEN Revodok Pro 7-in-1 is our top pick for dual 4K at 60Hz plus 100W passthrough in the lowest price tier. The Anker Nano 13-in-1 is the pick for three displays. The Anker Prime 14-Port is the pick for the most ports and up to 160W of output.
intro: A dock that says 8-in-1 can still leave your laptop underpowered, because the number on the box counts ports, not power delivery or monitor support. The wattage that reaches your laptop and the number of displays the dock can drive are the specs that decide whether it works for your desk.

We reviewed the eight docks against their listed ports, display support and power delivery, and ranked them on how much each gives you per price tier. HP business docks are included for office setups.

products.name: UGREEN 7-in-1 Docking Station (Revodok Pro)
products.verdict: Dual 4K at 60Hz and 100W passthrough at a $25-50 price.
products.description:
The Revodok Pro is a 7-in-1 USB-C hub with dual 4K at 60Hz HDMI outputs, 10Gbps data ports, 100W PD passthrough and an aluminum body.

It wins because it packs the specs that matter most, two sharp displays and strong power delivery, into the lowest price tier. The tradeoff versus the Anker docks is fewer ports and no Ethernet in the spec list.

It suits a two-monitor desk with a laptop that charges over USB-C. If you need wired networking, look further down.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want dual 4K and real 100W PD at the lowest possible price.
products.skipIf: You need Ethernet or an SD slot.

products.name: Anker Nano Laptop Docking Station 8-in-1
products.verdict: Dual 4K at 60Hz with an SD and TF card reader and 85W PD.
products.description:
This Anker Nano 8-in-1 offers dual monitor 4K at 60Hz HDMI, 10Gbps USB-C plus 2 USB-A ports, 85W PD and an SD/TF card reader.

It sits just behind the UGREEN because its 85W PD is lower than 100W, though it adds a card reader the UGREEN lacks. It is also in the $25-50 range.

It works for photographers and anyone offloading cards. Check that 85W covers your laptop's charger rating.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want an SD/TF card reader without paying more than $30.

products.name: Anker Laptop Docking Station 8-in-1
products.verdict: Gigabit Ethernet, two HDMI ports and an SD slot in an 8-in-1.
products.description:
This Anker 8-in-1 lists dual 4K monitor support over 2 HDMI ports, Gigabit Ethernet, 85W PD passthrough and an SD card slot.

It ranks third since it asks for $50-100 yet gives the same 85W as the cheaper Nano. What you gain is wired Ethernet, which the Nano and UGREEN lack.

It suits a desk that needs a stable wired connection. The listing does not state a 60Hz refresh rate, so check that for sharp motion.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want Ethernet and an SD slot without a big price jump.

products.name: Anker Nano 13-in-1 Laptop Docking Station
products.verdict: Three displays via 2 HDMI and 1 DisplayPort, with a detachable hub.
products.description:
The Nano 13-in-1 supports 3 displays at once through 2 HDMI ports and 1 DisplayPort, with 10Gbps USB-C, up to 100W PD and a detachable 6-in-1 hub in a compact modular design.

It ranks fourth because it costs more than the 8-in-1 docks, but it is the pick when two monitors are not enough. It stops short of the 14-port Prime's 160W.

Choose it for a triple-monitor desk. Make sure your laptop supports the display count.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want 3-display support without a full 14-port dock.
products.skipIf: You only use one or two monitors.

products.name: Anker Prime Docking Station 14-Port
products.verdict: 14 ports and up to 160W of output with independent PD circuitry.
products.description:
The Anker Prime has 14 ports in total, up to 160W maximum output, dual 4K display support, 10Gbps data throughput and independent PD circuitry.

It ranks fifth because the specs outclass the cheaper docks but the $100-200 price is steep for a single-laptop desk. It offers more power headroom than any other pick here.

It suits power-hungry laptops and desks with many peripherals. Smaller setups will not use all the ports.
products.idealFor: Buyers who need the highest PD wattage and the most ports in one dock.

products.name: Acer USB-C Docking Station 9-in-1
products.verdict: A compact 9-in-1 with two HDMI ports from a familiar brand.
products.description:
This Acer dock offers 9 ports, dual monitor support over 2 HDMI ports, a compact form factor and broad laptop compatibility, at $25-50.

It ranks sixth because the listing gives no wattage or 4K refresh rate, which the UGREEN and Anker docks do. You are buying the brand and port count.

It works for a basic desk where you do not need a stated power figure. Confirm charging wattage before relying on it.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a recognizable brand dock at a near-budget price.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed charging wattage.

products.name: HP USB-C Dock G5 11-in-1
products.verdict: A business 11-in-1 dock with firmware update support.
products.description:
The HP Dock G5 is a business-oriented 11-in-1 USB-C dock with firmware update support, designed for office desks and compatible with USB-C laptops beyond HP.

It ranks seventh because it is priced at $50-100 without a listed wattage or display spec, so it offers less measurable value than the Anker docks. Its edge is business-grade firmware support.

It suits IT-managed offices. Home buyers can get more listed specs for less elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Business laptop buyers who want HP's reliability and firmware support.
products.skipIf: You are a home user shopping on specs.

products.name: HP USB-C 100W G6 Dock
products.verdict: HP's current-generation G6 dock with genuine 100W PD.
products.description:
The HP G6 is a business-tier USB-C dock with 100W PD, firmware update support and a design built for the HP business laptop ecosystem.

It ranks last because the $100-200 price is high for a listing with no stated port count or display spec. It does list 100W, which the G5 does not.

It makes sense for an HP fleet that wants a vendor dock. Others will get more ports per dollar from the Anker options.
products.idealFor: Business buyers who want HP's own ecosystem dock with genuine 100W PD.
products.skipIf: You do not use HP laptops.

whatMatters.detail: PD passthrough charges your laptop through the dock, and the wattage must meet your laptop's needs. A dock below your charger's rating charges slowly or not at all. Check the PD number in the listing against your charger.
A dock can list dual monitor support but drive them at 30Hz, which feels sluggish. 4K at 60Hz is smooth. Look for the refresh rate in the specs.
Wired Ethernet gives a steadier connection than Wi-Fi for calls and large files. Not every dock includes it. Look for Gigabit Ethernet in the port list.
10Gbps ports move files from external drives much faster than older USB speeds. They matter if you use SSDs. Check for the 10Gbps mention.
The in-one number counts everything, including the input port. Count what you need, such as HDMI, USB-A and card slots. Match the list to your peripherals.

howToChoose.intro: Your monitor count narrows the field fast.

cards.label: Compact hub
cards.text: Fewer ports, lower cost and easier to carry. Picks: UGREEN Revodok Pro, Anker Nano 8-in-1 and Acer 9-in-1.

cards.label: Full dock
cards.text: More ports and power for fixed desks. Picks: Anker Prime 14-Port and Anker Nano 13-in-1.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to a compact hub like the UGREEN unless they run three screens or need 160W.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Firmware update support and broad USB-C compatibility so the dock works across laptop models.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The HP USB-C Dock G5 11-in-1 and HP USB-C 100W G6 Dock both list firmware update support.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You run three displays or a power-hungry laptop. The Anker Nano 13-in-1 and Anker Prime 14-Port cover those.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Two monitors and 100W are enough. The UGREEN Revodok Pro delivers both at $25-50.

faq.q: Will any USB-C dock work with my laptop?
faq.a: Not always. Docks need a USB-C port that supports video output and power delivery. Check your laptop's specs first.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying on the in-one number. Check wattage and display refresh rate, which decide real usability.

faq.q: Is the Anker Prime worth it over the UGREEN?
faq.a: Only if you need up to 160W output or 14 ports. The UGREEN handles dual 4K and 100W for much less.

faq.q: How do I set up dual monitors?
faq.a: Connect the dock to your laptop's USB-C port, plug the monitors into the HDMI ports and the charger into the dock. Then arrange displays in system settings.
Keep the dock ventilated and update firmware where supported. HP lists firmware updates.
Only if your laptop supports it. The Anker Nano 13-in-1 offers 2 HDMI and 1 DisplayPort for three displays.

finalTake: For most buyers, the UGREEN Revodok Pro is the best value because it covers dual 4K at 60Hz and 100W for $25-50. Add the Anker Nano 13-in-1 for three screens, or the Anker Prime for the most power and ports. HP docks suit office fleets.
